# The examples' config viewport becomes a workbench: stage, inspector, reset

## Context

The operator, Mon 16 Nov 2026 (relayed): some component examples look like a storybook; that part is to be upgraded significantly, into something like a storybook for Neo. On 10 Nov he had said of the config panel that it "could get enhanced a LOT" (Discussion #20744, which has had no comment since). A leaf of #21140, for the cut on Mon 23 Nov.

## The Problem

`examples/ConfigurationViewport.mjs` (233 lines on dev) carries 66 of the 139 runnable examples: every button, field, list, menu, tab and layout example. Each one is a small component at the top left of a white page beside a hand-written config panel. That every config is live is the engine's own kitchen-sink strength. As a page it reads as empty: in [the inventory](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20498#issuecomment-6918253093) these 66 frames are the white ones, and two readers without session context called their tiles toys.

## The Architectural Reality

- `examples/ConfigurationViewport.mjs`: 66 examples extend it and override `createConfigurationComponents()` (Discussion #20744's census; 75 files under `examples/` and `apps/` name the class on dev).
- The class has no reset of the whole example and no notion of a stage; the component sits where the layout puts it. It carries two theme buttons, one in the panel's header and one at its foot, which cycle three hard-coded themes. *(Corrected 16 Nov: this line said the class has no theme switch of its own; the released frames and `ConfigurationViewport.mjs` at 13.4.0, lines 159 to 184, show both.)*
- Design authority: the operator's words above; Discussion #20744 (ungraduated, an input).

## The Fix

1. **The look first, on this ticket** (the design seat, by Wed 18 Nov): three examples (a button, a form field, a list) as they render today beside the workbench, at 1440×900 and 390×844, in both themes. The operator reads the pair before anything is merged. *(Amended 16 Nov: PR #21154 from @mrdeyroy arrived two hours after this ticket, so its rendered candidate is the second half of the pair in place of a sketch; the design read and the operator's read gate the merge, not the build.)*
2. **Build it in the one class.** A stage that shows the component at a readable size on the theme's surface. The panel as an inspector, its configs grouped. A reset to the example's initial configs. A theme switch, with the Portal's theme as default. The 66 examples change without a change of their own.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.examples.ConfigurationViewport` | this ticket; the operator's direction of 16 Nov | stage, inspector, reset, theme | an example that overrides the layout keeps working, listed in the pull request | the class JSDoc | e2e on one example per kind |
| `createConfigurationComponents()` | the 66 examples | unchanged signature and return | none | unchanged | the examples load unchanged |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The pair is on this ticket and the operator's read is recorded.
- [ ] All 66 examples render through the new viewport; any that needed a change of its own is listed with the reason.
- [ ] Reset restores every config of the example to its initial value.
- [ ] The theme switch works in every example whose `neo-config.json` lists both themes.
- [ ] At 390×844 the component stays in view and the inspector opens below or over it.
- [ ] An e2e arm covers one button, one field and one list example: render, change a config, reset.
- [ ] The stage has one stable rect, so a cover recipe can capture any of the 66 with one rule.
- [ ] **Look:** the pull request shows three examples as released and as changed, and two readers without session context grade the unlabelled pair.

## Out of Scope

State in the URL, the config as code, an events view, a size switch (the next leaf); the examples' own content (the slate); an integration of Storybook (#5010).

## Avoided Traps

- **Restyling 66 files.** The class is the lever.
- **A new panel API.** `createConfigurationComponents()` stays; D#20744 lists richer options for later.
- **A dark page with the same tiny component.** The stage's size is the point.

**The look for this leaf starts from the candidate of PR #21154** · the design seat, Mon 16 Nov 2026

@mrdeyroy built the workbench two hours after this ticket went up. Thank you: a rendered candidate is better evidence than the sketch I owed for Wednesday, so it takes the sketch's place. The body's step 1 is amended: the design read and the operator's read gate the merge, not the build.

**Prior design work outside this ticket** (asked by Emmy): none. There is no board, no sketch and no operator read of a workbench look. The inputs are the two the ticket cites: his word of 10 Nov on the config panel ("could get enhanced a LOT") and of 16 Nov ("something like a storybook for Neo"), and Discussion #20744, closed into this leaf and #21144.

**The pair**, on this ticket: the three examples (`button/base`, `form/field/text`, `list/base`) as released and as changed, at 1440×900 and 390×844, in both themes, each as the whole window. Emmy has captured exactly that set; hers is the pair, no second capture.

**What I read it for**, so nobody iterates blind:

1. **The stage's size.** The component stands at a readable size on the theme's surface. A large empty stage with the same small component at its centre is the trap the ticket names.
2. **The inspector reads as one.** Configs grouped, labels aligned, and after Reset every control shows the value the component has.
3. **The theme switch** starts on the Portal's theme and offers the themes the example's `neo-config.json` lists.
4. **At 390×844** the component stays in view while a config changes.
5. **As a cover:** one stable rect that frames any of the 66 the same way.

**Who does what:** the formal code review is Emmy's, once CI is green; Grace's three points on the pull request stand. I post the design read here when the pair is up, with two readers without session context grading the unlabelled pair (the ticket's Look criterion). Then the operator reads it.

### @neo-fable-clio - 2026-11-16T17:01:03Z

**Design read of the candidate (PR #21154 at `3e217cba36`) on Emmy's twelve pairs: the lever works, the look is not there yet** · the design seat, Mon 16 Nov 2026

The pairs are [Emmy's](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21143#issuecomment-6922955561). I read them knowing the key. Two readers without session context read the 24 files unlabelled, in different orders; both told the two designs apart in all twelve pairs.

| Grade of 10 | An engineer who evaluates component libraries | A developer who tries components, half the time on a phone |
|---|---:|---:|
| Released, desktop | 4 | 5 |
| Released, phone | 4 | 4 |
| Candidate, desktop | 5 | 6 |
| Candidate, phone | 6 | 5 |

- Both prefer the candidate in 10 of 12 pairs, and the release in the two desktop button pairs, where the candidate's stage is empty.
- The engineer on both designs: they "read as dev scratchpads, not product pages". The developer on the candidate: "Stage ignores its content".
- Both name, unasked, what neither design has: the component's name, a line on what it is, a link to its docs or source.
- On the phone the developer would rather change the text field's settings in the release: 19 settings in view against 14.
- Limits: stills only, so Reset and the theme switch were not exercised; the readers had the 24 files and nothing else.

**Against the five points**

1. **The stage's size: not met, and it is the trap the ticket names.** The component has the size it had; it moved from the top left to the centre of a 925 × 860 box. The text field is 200 px wide in it, the list 100 px. Nothing became more readable, and at cover size the component is a speck. On the phone the stage is 240 px high and the proportion is nearer. In the dark theme the stage's border and fill barely separate from the page.
2. **The inspector reads as one: not yet.** The header is better (a title, Reset, the theme). The configs are the same flat list where the ticket asks for groups. The two buttons at the foot stayed, so there are two theme buttons whose labels disagree in the dark frames (header "Theme Neo-Light", foot "Theme Dark"). The text field shows a header Reset above its own `reset()` button. "Log Instance" is cut off at the foot of the text field's panel. After Reset the controls keep their old values (Emmy's finding). On the phone the header buttons are about 13 px high.
3. **The theme switch: unchanged.** The released class already had the header button and the foot button, cycling three hard-coded themes. The ticket asks for the Portal's theme first and the themes the example's `neo-config.json` lists. The ticket said the class had no theme switch of its own; that was my error and is corrected in the body.
4. **At 390 × 844: better for the field and the list, broken for the button.** Open, since a still cannot show it: whether the stage stays in view while a config further down changes.
5. **As a cover: not one rect.** 925 × 860 on the desktop; on the phone 240 px for two examples and the whole screen for the button.

**The button, in both themes:** on the desktop the stage is empty, on the phone it takes the whole first screen and the inspector is out of sight. The cause is the example, not the viewport: `examples/button/base/MainContainer.mjs` gives its button `marginTop: '500px'` and `marginBottom: '1500px'`, a scroll test inside a visitor example. It is the first of the 66 that needs a change of its own (criterion 2), and a row for the slate (#21142).

**What I ask of the next head, in this order**

1. The stage takes its size from the component, on the desktop as on the phone: one fixed, modest rect in which the component is at least a third of the width, and a surface that reads as one in both themes.
2. The page says what it shows: the component's name and one line, in the stage's header. Both readers asked for it.
3. One theme control and one Reset; the foot buttons go. Reset also resets the controls. On the phone a finger can hit them.
4. The configs in groups. Without touching 66 examples the control type can carry it (flags, sizes, text, choices); an optional `group` on an item can follow.
5. `button/base` loses its two margins, listed as its own change.
6. On the phone the stage stays in view while the inspector scrolls.

@mrdeyroy: the direction is right, and building it in the one class proved the lever in two hours. None of the six is a rewrite; the candidate already wins ten of twelve pairs against the release.

**For the operator's read:** the pairs, the grades and this list. The candidate stands at 5 and 6 against the release's 4 to 5, under the bar of 9 that the examples section carries (#21140). His read is this ticket's first criterion.

## Second design read: `013f61efbc`, with a sketch of where the six asks lead

**Two of the six asks are met, four are open, and the first screen loads unstyled. This head is not ready for the operator's read before merge.** Two heads have now answered a list of constraints, so this read adds what the first one lacked: one frame of the target, for the operator to read beside the candidate.

Read on [Emmy's pairs](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21143#issuecomment-6926826059): nine frames of the candidate opened at full size (three examples on the desktop, three on the phone, the dark list, the first load).

| # | Ask of the [first read](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21143#issuecomment-6923206618) | At `013f61efbc` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The stage takes its size from the component | **Phone: met.** One rect of 370 × 280 for all three. **Desktop: open.** The stage is about 920 × 860 and the component sits in its top left corner: the button is 16 % of the stage's width, the field 22 %, the list 11 %. |
| 2 | The component's name and one line, in the stage's header | **Open.** "Inspector" is the only title on the page. |
| 3 | One theme control, one Reset that also resets the controls | **Met.** The foot buttons are gone, and Emmy's Chromium run shows Reset remounting all three. Left over: on the phone both header buttons are about 14 px high; the text field keeps a second `RESET()` at the inspector's foot; the theme button still cycles three hard-coded themes. |
| 4 | The configs in groups | **Open.** One alphabetical list. |
| 5 | `button/base` loses its two margins | **Met.** The button is in view on both sizes. |
| 6 | On the phone the stage stays in view while the inspector scrolls | **Open** (Emmy's run). |
| new | The first screen | **Blocking.** The examples set `neo-theme-neo-dark` without loading its stylesheet: Times on a white page, the badge printed over the button's text ([capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neomjs/neo/3d710c0c0143cd940cd585862451b97d2789e4ca/review-evidence/21143/repair-013f61e/button-base-desktop-default.png)). |

### The sketch

A static page for `button/base` at both sizes ([source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3eb484370b78b9b56244a3295621cdf9d0d28bc9/review-evidence/21143/sketch-2026-11-16/sketch.html)). **It is the direction this slice takes** (decided 16 Nov, 19:55Z, by the design seat while the operator is away): the next head builds toward it. The operator reads the pair at his merge gate on PR #21154, which this ticket's first criterion asks for, and an objection there changes the direction.

| The candidate | The sketch |
|---|---|
| ![candidate, desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neomjs/neo/3d710c0c0143cd940cd585862451b97d2789e4ca/review-evidence/21143/repair-013f61e/button-base-desktop-light-a.png) | ![sketch, desktop](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3eb484370b78b9b56244a3295621cdf9d0d28bc9/review-evidence/21143/sketch-2026-11-16/sketch-button-desktop.png?raw=true) |
| ![candidate, phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neomjs/neo/3d710c0c0143cd940cd585862451b97d2789e4ca/review-evidence/21143/repair-013f61e/button-base-phone-light-b.png) | ![sketch, phone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3eb484370b78b9b56244a3295621cdf9d0d28bc9/review-evidence/21143/sketch-2026-11-16/sketch-button-phone.png?raw=true) |

What it shows, by ask: a stage card of 480 × 300 with the component centred on one ground (1) · a header with the component's name, its class and one line, plus Source and API docs (2) · the inspector in four groups by control type: text, choices, sizes, flags, which needs no change in the 66 examples (4) · on the phone the stage stays pinned and carries the theme switch and Reset at finger size ([scrolled](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3eb484370b78b9b56244a3295621cdf9d0d28bc9/review-evidence/21143/sketch-2026-11-16/sketch-button-phone-scrolled.png?raw=true)) (3, 6). The class name is free at runtime; the one line is an optional config on the example.

### Cold look

One reader without context, six unlabelled frames in shuffled order, as an engineer evaluating a component library:

| | Released 13.4.0 | Candidate | Sketch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Desktop, 1440 × 900 | 3 | 4 | 7 |
| Phone, 390 × 844 | 2 | 4 | 8 |

The reader ranks the candidate above the release on both sizes ("a framed stage and an Inspector with Reset give some structure, but the button is lost in an empty frame and nothing says what this is"). What keeps the sketch from 9, in the reader's order: no copyable code of the current config, which the reader calls what they need to adopt the component; one small state in the stage beside a wide inspector, with unequal columns; no word on whether theme and Reset act on the page or the component, and numbers without units. All three versions lack a way back to the examples and any variant beside the default.

The first of these is #21144's subject. I re-cut that leaf with the workbench's look on Wed 18 Nov, so the code pane can follow this slice directly instead of after the release.

### Asked of the next head

1. The first screen loads its theme. Nothing else is read before that.
2. The stage as a fixed, modest rect with the component centred, and a header that names it.
3. The inspector in groups by control type.
4. On the phone: the stage pinned, the two controls in its header at 44 px.

The second `RESET()` on the text field calls the field's own method; label it so, or it reads as a duplicate.

**For the operator:** the pair above is the read this ticket's first criterion asks for. It waits at the merge gate of PR #21154, on the head built toward the sketch; nothing merges before it.
